Every sold call/custom must have fan, amount, duration and exact promises written down before the fan is told anything, and one voice must own that fan. 'Can you please answer whats going on??😥' was the sound of a client losing trust in real time, and it was never followed up with an apology or a process change.

2026-08-04 and 2026-08-10 — Three traffic promises in six days ('48 hrs', 'its live', 'another hour and ill answer you'), none delivered, none evidenced. Any promise with a stated deadline should be tracked and either delivered or explicitly retracted. Derrek made the last of these and then left the chat entirely — the owner going quiet immediately after over-promising is the single clearest churn accelerant in this file.

2026-08-11 to 2026-08-17 — She asked whether the same complaint was solved THREE TIMES in six days and got 'Looking into this for you', 'Yes that one was solved', 'Yes all solved' — three assertions, zero evidence. This is the rule the whole book needs: a client asking 'is this solved?' a third time is an active churn case that week, and complaints must be closed with evidence (numbers, screenshots, dates), never with a claim. She terminated 18 hours after 'Yes all solved'.

2026-08-17 — 'is it possible for you to count from 1st- 18th ?' is a client asking for her final bill. Nobody recognised it. A mid-cycle request for a partial-period total should always be treated as an exit signal and escalated to the owner before the invoice is prepared.

2026-08-18 — The termination itself. She asked for two things and got a file with no words and then, eight days later, a bare collections line. Any churned client must get an owner message within 24 hours, BEFORE any collections message, and every churn must trigger an asset-and-access offboarding checklist — Infloww disconnect, Drive access, custom domain, managed IG account, chatter cutoff date, and outstanding fan-money liabilities — rather than depending on someone remembering.

top_fix: Close complaints with evidence, not assertions — and never switch off a client's own working revenue source until the replacement is live and measured. Those two changes alone would have saved this account: she left because she funded her own traffic, was told to stop it, waited 51 days for a replacement she was never shown a single number for, and then heard 'Yes all solved' about a page with no fans.
